title: The goal line is closed to a held puck: a goal must leave a blade by a shot or a pass
hypothesis: E01 showed the idea works and the first rule leaked. The rule now remembers who holds the puck: once it has ridden with a skater it is his until he shoots it, passes it or another skater touches it, and while it is his the goal mouth is a wall for it (a deflection, a rebound and a puck off a defender score as before). Expected: no goal by a skater who has not released the puck, for every hand and both sides (T1); a hand without any shot scores almost nothing (T2: at least 30 points of wins lost at pro, from 8); the planning hand turns its walk-ins into shots and loses little; thirdjam's scripted hand, which cannot re-plan, loses its walked goals and some wins; possession, carries and knockdowns do not move.
tempo: none: no row of the tempo map moves (the gym probes are equal)

table: | cell | win % | goal diff | gf/min | ga/min | walk-in goals / match | shots/min | pass compl % | passes/min | one-timers / match | carry s | carries lost % | takes key / no key per min | knockdowns | down s | changes/min | match s | paired: wins pp, goal diff |

why: T1 met: no goal by a skater who had not released the puck, in every full-hand cell, both sides (thirdjam's regular hand at pro walked in 18 % of its side's goals before, the planning hand's side 5 %; the opponents 0-5 %). T2 met: taking every shot away now costs thirdjam's regular hand 35 points of wins at pro (63.3 -> 28.3; before 75 -> 66.7, 8 points) and the planning hand 58 (85 -> 26.7; before 8). The price is on the hand that cannot re-plan: thirdjam's regular hand loses 11.7 points at pro (75 -> 63.3, paired, 2.4 standard errors) because it still skates at the line; the planning hand, which turns the walk-in into a tap, does not lose (76.7 -> 85, +8.3 +-6.0). Nothing else moved beyond noise: carries, passes, possession as before; matches 5-10 % longer (fewer cheap goals), so knockdowns a match rise with them (4.1 -> 4.5). Still dead after it: the deke (83.3 against 85 without it). The tap went from costing the planning hand (88.3 without it against 76.7) to neutral (81.7 against 85).
owner_line: A breakaway now ends with a press. Glide the puck at the net and it stops on the goal line and lies there; tap shoot (a tap is enough) and it is in. The opponents cannot walk it in on you either.
notes: "walk-in goals / match" in the table is K4's count (the hand's carry was still open on the goal frame); after the rule that count is point-blank taps and passes that cross the line on the frame they leave the blade. The strict count (the puck rode with a skater at the end of the frame before and he had not shot or passed for 45 frames: goals_walk in the JSON) is 0 of every full hand's goals; 1.1 % and 3.8 % in the two no-shot cells. Traced on 24 Nov (rinklab-thirdlife -debuggoals, thirdjam's regular hand without shots at pro, seeds 1-60): 226 goals, none with a holder; the 3 that the strict count calls walked are the human standing on the goal line with the puck and an opposing defender's stick knocking it into his own net (last toucher an opponent): a puck off a defender, which scores by the rule as written. A thing to watch, not a leak. 60 seeds a cell. Parity of the patched tree with the switch off: rink.sh balance-thirdlife --parity, PASS, 600 of 600 hashes. The patch has three parts and the experiment measured the third form: a second form (held until released, without the last guard) was spot-checked on six rookie matches without shots before any cell ran and still leaked: the carry's pull drew the puck round a post towards a blade that was already inside the net and the net's side wall pushed it in (rinklab -debuggoals: every leaked goal lay 1.83-1.88 m off the axis, held by its scorer). The guard that puts a held puck back out of the net closed it: 0 goals by a holder in eight such matches.
